title: JSX and Components
subtitle: The Language of React - How to Build Reusable Lego Blocks
description: Master JSX syntax, all JSX rules, JavaScript inside JSX, functional components, composition, fragments, styling in React, and how to structure components like real companies do.

blocks.text: PAGE 1: Welcome - Where Real React Starts

PAGE 2: What is JSX? Not HTML, Not JavaScript

JSX = JavaScript XML. It's a syntax extension that lets you write HTML-like code INSIDE JavaScript. Example: const element =

Hello

; This line is NOT HTML, it's JSX. React converts it behind the scenes to React.createElement('h1', null, 'Hello').

Why did Facebook invent JSX? Because they realized: Logic and UI belong together. In old days we separated HTML, CSS, JS in different files. But for a Button, the logic (what happens when clicked), the UI (how it looks), and the state (is it loading?) are all related. JSX puts them together in one component file.
JSX looks like HTML but has superpowers: You can embed JavaScript, use components, and write dynamic UIs. It's not a string, it's not HTML - it's syntactic sugar for React.createElement.

blocks.text: PAGE 3: The 7 Golden Rules of JSX - Must Know

Rule 1: Return ONE parent element. You cannot return

and

or Fragment <> .
Rule 2: class becomes className. Because class is a reserved keyword in JavaScript. So <div class='box'> in HTML becomes <div className='box'> in JSX.

Rule 3: All tags must be closed. must be or .
becomes
. In HTML you could leave it open, in JSX you cannot.

Rule 4: camelCase for attributes. onclick becomes onClick, onchange becomes onChange, tabindex becomes tabIndex. Rule 5: Use {} for JavaScript expressions. Rule 6: Style is an object, not string. Rule 7: Comments are {/* comment */} not <!-- comment -->.

blocks.question: In JSX, what do you use instead of class?
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! className because class is reserved in JavaScript. This trips every beginner.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: In JSX it's className, not class. Example: <div className='box'>
blocks.reasoning: JSX attribute naming follows JavaScript camelCase and reserved words avoidance.

blocks.text: PAGE 4: JavaScript Inside JSX - The {} Magic

This is what makes JSX powerful. Anything inside {} is executed as JavaScript. You can put variables, calculations, function calls, ternary operators, map(). You CANNOT put if statements or for loops directly inside {} - you need to put them outside or use ternary/map.

blocks.title: Example 4: What You CANNOT Do Inside {}

blocks.question: Can you put an if statement directly inside JSX {}?
options: Yes, you can write if() inside {}
No, you must use ternary? : or && or move logic outside
No, JSX doesn't allow any JavaScript
blocks.correctFeedback: Exactly! if/for cannot go inside JSX directly. Use ternary or map().
blocks.incorrectFeedback: You cannot put if/for inside {}. Use ternary: {condition? <A/> : <B/>} or map().
blocks.reasoning: JSX {} only accepts expressions, not statements like if/for.

blocks.text: PAGE 5: What is a Component? Your Lego Block

A Component is a function that returns JSX. That's it! But there are rules: Name MUST start with Capital Letter (Header not header), must return JSX (or null), and can be reused. There are two types but we use Functional Components - modern standard.

Why components? Imagine your Code Academy app dashboard from Page you gave me - that beautiful page with course-icon, hero, lesson-grid, lesson-card. Each of those is a component! You build LessonCard once, and you reuse it 10 times for 10 lessons with different data. That's why React is scalable.

blocks.text: PAGE 6: Composition & Reusability - The Real Power

Composition means building big components from small ones. This is how you reach your Lesson 10 target - complete app. You don't build one huge App.jsx with 500 lines. You build small pieces and compose them.

blocks.title: Example 6: Composition - Building Dashboard Like Yours

blocks.question: What is Composition in React?
options: Writing all code in one big file
Building big components by combining smaller reusable components
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes! Like Lego - small blocks combine to build big app. That's how you will build Lesson 10 project.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Composition = Small components + Small components = Big component. Like Header + Hero + LessonGrid = Dashboard.
blocks.reasoning: Composition is core to scalable React architecture.

blocks.text: PAGE 7: Fragments and Why We Need Them

Remember Rule 1: Return ONE parent. But sometimes you don't want extra <div> in HTML because it breaks styling. Example: Your lesson-grid needs direct children lesson-card, not wrapped in div. Solution: Fragment - <></> or <React.Fragment>. It doesn't create extra DOM element.

blocks.text: PAGE 8: Styling in JSX - 3 Ways Professionals Use

Way 1: Inline style object - style={{color: 'red'}}. Notice double {{}} - outer {} for JS, inner {} for object. Way 2: className with CSS file - import './App.css' then className='card'. Way 3: CSS Modules / Tailwind (we will use in Lesson 9). For your dashboard you used CSS variables --react, --bg - that's professional Way 2.

blocks.title: Example 8: Styling Like Your Dashboard - Professional Way

blocks.question: How do you write inline style in JSX?
options: style={{color: 'red'}} - object with double braces and camelCase
blocks.incorrectFeedback: It's style={{color: 'red'}} - outer {} for JS, inner {} for style object, camelCase properties.
blocks.reasoning: JSX style is JavaScript object, not CSS string.

blocks.text: PAGE 9: Organizing Components Like a Pro - Folder Structure

Don't put all components in one file. Real companies do this: src/components/Header.jsx, src/components/LessonCard.jsx, src/components/Hero.jsx. Each component in its own file, then import where needed. This is how you keep your Lesson 10 final project clean and scalable.

PAGE 12: Common Mistakes & How to Debug
Mistake 1: Forgetting to export/import - You create Header.jsx but forget export default Header, then App cannot find it. Error: Component not defined. Fix: Always export.

Mistake 2: Small letter component - function header() will not work, React thinks it's HTML tag. Always Capital. Mistake 3: Returning multiple elements without wrapper - use <> fragment. Mistake 4: Using class instead of className - React will warn you.

blocks.text: PAGE 14: Summary & Next Lesson

You mastered today: What JSX is (JS + HTML-like syntax that compiles to React.createElement), 7 golden rules (one parent, className, closed tags, camelCase, {} for JS, style object, comments), embedding JavaScript inside JSX, functional components (capital letter, return JSX), composition (small + small = big), fragments <> to avoid extra div, styling with className and style object, file organization with components/ folder, and conditional rendering with ternary and &&.

In Lesson 4 you will add state to make progress bar interactive. By Lesson 10 you combine all into complete React app like your dashboard.
